title: register_price_dispute
beats: I (19F) just fixed a $2 price error at my register. That's it. That's the story. Except it isn't.
Guy at checkout points out sunglasses ring up $8.99 but the sticker says $6.99.
I can't override prices myself, only a manager can log into the POS with their badge.
I grab my supervisor (24F) to fix it, simple enough, right?
She stares at the screen, then whispers to me, 'I don't know how to do it.'
I start saying 'I can-' but she cuts me off and tells the customer he has to pay full price.
He is NOT having it, starts raising his voice, and now there's a line forming.
I ask her to just scan her badge so I can fix it myself under her login.
She does, I change it in ten seconds, customer pays and leaves happy.
Then she rips into me IN FRONT of other customers for 'making her look stupid.'
I said, 'You didn't know how to change the price, so I did it. What's the big deal?'
She snapped: 'You threw me under the bus to make yourself look good. You're selfish.'
I said, 'I'm selfish for doing your job that you couldn't?' She just walked away.
I know that last line was harsh, but she started it by attacking me first. So, Reddit... AITAH?
